notes:
Summary: SafeCode builds an IDE copilot targeting enterprise dev teams. Primary ask: tool/function-calling for code agents — run unit tests, linters, static analysis, capture build logs and stream back to the editor with sub-100ms typing/stream latency. Must support model/version pinning per workspace and deterministic fallbacks (pinned model -> smaller local quantized model) for offline dev.

Security & sandboxing: they require ephemeral, network-restricted execution (k8s pods or Firecracker-type microVMs), strict file system mounts, and no persistent artifacts outside a sealed artifact store. "We can't risk remote code execution touching internal repos" — Head of Security. Want attestation/KMS-wrapped keys for any artifact access.

POC scope: integrate Redwood function-calling to invoke a test-runner toolchain (pytest/go test), capture stdout/stderr, provide structured test results and timeline, surface linter suggestions as structured function outputs for the copilot to render actionable fixes. POC also to test streaming chunking to the IDE (low-latency) and model pin + fallback behavior when private infra flips to offline.

Performance constraints: median gen latency for inline completions < 50ms (edge batching acceptable), streaming token latency < 20ms for interactive sessions, per-request cold-start for ephemeral runner < 400ms. Throughput: 5k test-run calls/day across 100 devs initially. Cost sensitivity: moderate — willing to pay premium for guarded execution and SLA but want Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce token spend.

Compliance: SOC2 + ISO27001 important; wanting audit logs, request-level retention controls, and per-team data residency. Legal: wants no customer code stored in hosted cache unless explicitly allowed.

Quotes / call snippets: "If the test runner can stream logs to the editor and we can pin a model per team, we can replace our expensive host-based copilot stack." — VP Eng.

Open items: installer package size limit for on-prem, E2E threat model for function execution, benchmark for pinned model fallback latency, pricing for high-throughput ephemeral containers.

Next steps (internal): SE to prepare POC runbook + threat model checklist; AE to coordinate legal DPA + MSA redlines; schedule 1-week smoke test then full 2-week POC.
